note: Known-answer gate corpus for College Football Comparator (FBS players, 2004 season onward). A row gets in only when a publisher's exact number for a player-season, career, game or window is quoted verbatim from a saved copy of a page (research/factoids-players/pages, keyed by sha1(url)) and scripts/check-receipts.mjs finds every quote. The build recomputes each row's value from ESPN per-game box scores under the row's window and scope and fails on a mismatch; where the publisher's definition differs from what box scores can express (sacks in rushing, vacated stats, FCS seasons, starts, class year, position), the row's notes say so and the gate should word the difference in Method rather than patch data. NCAA rows cite the current FBS record book (records through the 2025 season); per the book, all postseason games are included in season and career totals since 2002.

rejections.claim: Jeremiah Smith (Ohio State) broke the FBS freshman receiving record in 2024.
rejections.reason: Wikipedia's lead says so, but the NCAA FBS record book's freshman receiving-yards record is Michael Crabtree's 1,962 (2007) and Smith had 1,315; freshman receptions record is Crabtree's 134 (Smith 76). The Wikipedia claim is either a true-freshman or school/conference record mislabeled. Not a gate.

receipts.quote: As a college freshman in 2024, Smith broke the NCAA Division I Football Bowl Subdivision (FBS) freshman receiving record, and won a national championship with the Buckeyes.

rejections.claim: Bo Nix holds the record for most career starts (61).
rejections.reason: Superseded: NCAA's Most Games Started list has Dillon Gabriel (QB) at 63 and two non-QBs at 65; Nix's 61 is not in the list. Also starts are not derivable from box scores.

receipts.quote: He started 61 games between Auburn and Oregon, the most in NCAA history for a quarterback.

rejections.claim: Jordan Lynch's 1,920 rushing yards (2013) is the FBS season record for a quarterback.
rejections.reason: True when set; now Malcolm Perry's 2,017 (Navy, 2019). Kept as a row with the corrected framing (lynch-2013-qb-rush), rejected as worded.

rejections.claim: Melvin Gordon's 408 yards vs Nebraska is the FBS single-game rushing record.
rejections.reason: Stood one week; Samaje Perine's 427 (Nov. 22, 2014) is the record. Kept as a row with correct framing.

receipts.quote: 427—Samaje Perine, Oklahoma vs. Kansas, Nov. 22, 2014 (34 rushes)

rejections.claim: Tim Tebow (2007) was the first FBS player with 20 rushing and 20 passing touchdowns in a season (as a clean 'first').
rejections.reason: Rejected as an unqualified 'first': the NCAA list's criterion is rushing+receiving TD, and Dan LeFevour also qualified in 2007 (19 rush + 1 rec + 27 pass). Tebow is first if the criterion is 20 rushing TD only. Row kept (tebow-2007-20-20) with that note.

receipts.quote: Dan LeFevour, Central Mich., 2007 (19 rushing, 1 receiving, 27 passing)

rejections.claim: Case Keenum career passing TDs is the sole FBS record (seed implied).
rejections.reason: Tied: Dillon Gabriel 155 (2024). Both kept as rows.
